mainTopic: Which offerings a גוי may bring: the מחלוקת between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא, and the source for רבי שמעון's rule about a כהן's מנחת חוטא.
overview: This amud opens with the rule that a גוי's שלמים are offered as עולות and burned completely. The גמרא supports the rule with logic (a גוי's heart is fully for Heaven) and with the פסוק "אשר יקריבו לה׳ לעולה". רבא answers a challenge from a ברייתא by explaining that it is talking about שלמים a גוי brought for a Jew's atonement. רבי יוחנן answers a second challenge, from a גוי's מנחה, by showing that the two sources follow a מחלוקת. רבי יוסי הגלילי lets a גוי bring almost any offering except a נזיר's. רבי עקיבא allows only an עולה. The גמרא then shows that sources about a גוי's נסכים can fit either view, because רבי עקיבא's עולה includes everything that goes with it. Finally the גמרא turns to רבי שמעון's rule about a כהן's מנחת חוטא. A ברייתא gives the first reading of the פסוק, and רבי שמעון begins his own reading, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A gentile's peace offerings become burnt offerings
steps.stepSummary: The rule: שלמים brought by a גוי are offered as עולות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Peace offerings of a gentile are burnt offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule. If a גוי brings שלמים, they are sacrificed as עולות and burned completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew's שלמים are partly eaten by the owner and the כהנים. A גוי's שלמים get a different outcome: they are offered entirely on the מזבח, like an עולה. The rest of the section explains and defends this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings. Usually parts are eaten by the owner and the כהנים.
Burnt offering(s), burned completely on the מזבח.
A non-Jew.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גוי's animal somehow 'isn't a valid offering.' It is accepted, but it is brought as an עולה instead of being eaten.

phrases.english: Peace offerings of a gentile are burnt offerings,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by restating the rule being discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי's שלמים are offered as עולות and are not eaten.

steps.title: Two possible sources, starting with logic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the rule can come from a פסוק or from logic. It explains the logic first: a גוי's heart is fully for Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say a verse; and if you want, say a logical reason. If you want, say a logical reason: a gentile's heart is directed to Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up two ways to support the rule, a פסוק or logic. It begins with the logic: when a גוי brings an offering, his intention is for it to go entirely to Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is about the גוי's intention. He means to give the whole animal to Heaven, not to share in eating it. So the offering is treated as fully burned, which makes it an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say... (introduces one of two possible explanations).
A verse from the תורה.
A logical argument.
His heart is directed to Heaven.

phrases.english: If you want, say a verse,
and if you want, say a logical reason.
If you want, say a logical reason:
a gentile's heart is directed to Heaven.
phrases.notes: He means the גוי wants the whole animal to go to Heaven, not for any of it to be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first reason for the rule in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Logically, a גוי's offering is meant entirely for Heaven, so it is fully burned.

steps.title: The verse-based source
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "אשר יקריבו לה׳ לעולה" teaches that whatever offering a גוי brings becomes an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say a verse: "which they will offer to ה׳ as a burnt offering". Whatever they offer should be a burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the second source, a פסוק. It reads the verse as saying that every offering these people bring should be an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse talks about offerings brought by people who include non-Jews. It ends with the word "לעולה". The גמרא reads that ending as a general rule: any offering they bring, even one they called שלמים, is an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: They will offer.
That they offer.
Let it be / it should be.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for the rule. The logic is that a גוי's heart is for Heaven. The פסוק is "אשר יקריבו לה׳ לעולה".

phrases.english: And if you want, say a verse:
"which they will offer to ה׳ as a burnt offering":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:18

phrases.english: anything they offer should be a burnt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second option that was promised in step 2: a פסוק instead of logic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק makes every offering of a גוי into an עולה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a gentile's peace offerings are eaten
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר גוריא challenges the rule from a ברייתא. It says that a גוי's שלמים, once given to a ישראל or a כהן, are eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר גוריא objects: A gentile who volunteered to bring peace offerings: if he gave them to an Israelite, the Israelite eats them; if he gave them to a priest, the priest eats them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא בר גוריא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the rule. In that ברייתא, a גוי's שלמים are eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1 to 3 said a גוי's שלמים become עולות, which are never eaten. This ברייתא says a ישראל or a כהן eats them. That looks like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Volunteered (pledged an offering of his own free will).
He gave them.
Eats them.

phrases.english: Rav Chama bar Gurya raises an objection:
A gentile who volunteered to bring peace offerings:
if he gave them to an Israelite, the Israelite eats them;
if he gave them to a priest, the priest eats them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule taught in steps 1 to 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a גוי's שלמים are עולות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a גוי's שלמים were really עולות, nobody could eat them. The ברייתא says they are eaten.

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא is about atoning for a Jew
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the ברייתא. The גוי brought the שלמים to provide atonement for a ישראל or a כהן, so that person eats them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what it is saying. If it was so that an Israelite would gain atonement through them, the Israelite eats them. If it was so that a priest would gain atonement through them, the priest eats them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by rereading the ברייתא. "Gave them to" means the גוי brought the offering on behalf of a Jew, so it counts as that Jew's שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not about a גוי's own offering. It is about a גוי who brings שלמים for a ישראל or a כהן so that the Jew gains atonement. Because the offering really belongs to the Jew, it follows normal שלמים rules and is eaten. A גוי's own שלמים still become עולות.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying (rereading a source).
On condition that / for the purpose of.
That he should gain atonement.

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי's own שלמים become עולות. If a גוי brings שלמים for a Jew's atonement, they are that Jew's שלמים and are eaten normally.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what it is saying:
if it was so that an Israelite would gain atonement through them,
phrases.notes: This is רבא's reading of "he gave them to an Israelite" in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: the Israelite eats them;
if it was so that a priest would gain atonement through them,
the priest eats them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that a גוי's own שלמים are eaten.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about שלמים brought for a Jew's atonement, so they are the Jew's and are eaten. A גוי's own שלמים remain עולות.

steps.title: A challenge from the meal offering of non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי challenges the rule from a משנה. It says a גוי's מנחה has a handful removed and the כהנים eat the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי objects: The משנה lists the מנחות from which a handful is taken and the rest is eaten by the כהנים, and the list includes the מנחה of a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge is brought against the rule that a גוי's שלמים are offered entirely as עולות. This time the source is a משנה about מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהנים eat the leftover of a גוי's מנחה, then a גוי's offerings are clearly treated like a Jew's. So why should his שלמים be burned completely as an עולה instead of being eaten?

keyTerms.meaning: Meal offerings made of flour
Have a handful (קומץ) removed and burned on the מזבח
The leftover part of the מנחה after the handful is taken

phrases.english: Rav Sheizevi raises an objection:
These are the meal offerings from which a handful is taken
and their leftovers go to the kohanim:
the meal offering of non-Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the same rule, after רבא answered the first one in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a גוי's שלמים are offered as עולות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גוי's מנחה is eaten by כהנים like a Jew's מנחה. So his שלמים should also be eaten and not turned into an עולה.

steps.title: The two sources follow two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי and the rule follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This is not a problem. One source is רבי יוסי הגלילי, and the other is רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן does not try to make both sources agree. He says they come from two תנאים who disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, a גוי's offerings are eaten like a Jew's, so his מנחה leftovers go to the כהנים. According to רבי עקיבא, a גוי's שלמים become עולות. The contradiction disappears because each source follows a different view.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the contradiction can be resolved
This one ... that one: assigning each source to a different opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: It is not difficult.
This one is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה, where the כהנים eat a גוי's מנחה.

phrases.english: that one is Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: He means the rule from step 1, that a גוי's שלמים become עולות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שיזבי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the two sources to two disagreeing תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the rule seemed to be one view that contradicts itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי and the rule follows רבי עקיבא. They simply disagree.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule from step 1 is now shown to be only one side of a מחלוקת תנאים, not something everyone agrees on.

steps.title: The double word 'איש איש' includes non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show the מחלוקת. The doubled word 'איש איש' teaches that a גוי can bring נדרים and נדבות like a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: The פסוק could have said 'a man'. Why does it say 'a man, a man'? To include non-Jews, who can pledge vow offerings and gift offerings just like a Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן's answer. It begins by proving that non-Jews can bring offerings at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra word in the פסוק is read as coming to add something. Here the extra 'איש' adds non-Jews to the people who may bring נדרים and נדבות. This is the base the ברייתא builds on before it lists which kinds of offerings are included.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says (used to point to the exact wording being learned from)
To include something extra
Vow offerings: 'I take upon myself to bring an offering'
Gift offerings: 'This animal is an offering'

phrases.english: As it was taught: "A man" would have been enough;
why does the verse say "a man, a man"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:18

phrases.english: To include the non-Jews,
who can pledge vow offerings and gift offerings like a Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that backs up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the two sources follow a מחלוקת between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: A גוי can bring עולה, שלמים and תודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the words 'נדריהם' and 'נדבותם' that a גוי can bring שלמים and a תודה, not only an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'which they will offer to ה׳ as an עולה'. From this I would only know about an עולה. How do we know שלמים? The פסוק says 'their vows'. How do we know a תודה? The פסוק says 'their gift offerings'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It shows that a גוי may bring other kinds of offerings besides an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לעולה' alone would limit a גוי to עולות. The extra words 'נדריהם' and 'נדבותם' widen this to include שלמים and תודה. This part of the ברייתא treats a גוי's שלמים as real שלמים, unlike the rule from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only know (the simple case), before the extra words add more
From where do we know?
Thanks offering

steps.confusionAlert: Earlier, in step 3, the same words 'אשר יקריבו לה׳ לעולה' were used to say that everything a גוי brings becomes an עולה. Here the ברייתא reads the פסוק differently, so that a גוי can also bring שלמים and תודה. These are two different views.

phrases.english: "Which they will offer to ה׳ as a burnt offering":
from this I would know only about a burnt offering.
From where do we know peace offerings?
The verse says "their vows."
From where do we know a thanks offering?
The verse says "their gift offerings."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עוֹלָה, שְׁלָמִים מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and lists which offerings a גוי may bring.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי may bring an עולה, שלמים and a תודה.

steps.title: A גוי can also bring birds, wine, frankincense and wood
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the extra words 'לכל נדריהם' and 'לכל נדבותם' that a גוי can also donate birds, wine, frankincense and wood for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know to include birds, wine, frankincense and wood? The פסוק says 'their vows' and also 'all their vows', and 'their gift offerings' and also 'all their gift offerings'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes one step further. It includes even smaller donations to the מזבח that a גוי may give.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already used 'נדריהם' and 'נדבותם' for שלמים and תודה. The added word 'לכל' (all) widens it even more, to birds, wine, frankincense and wood. The ברייתא continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Bird offerings
Frankincense
Wood donated for the fire on the מזבח
'All': a wider word that includes even more

phrases.english: From where do we know to include birds,
and wine, and frankincense, and wood?
The verse says "their vows," and also "all their vows,"
"their gift offerings," and also "all their gift offerings."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת הָעוֹפוֹת, וְהַיַּיִן, וְהַלְּבוֹנָה, וְהָעֵצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and widens the list of what a גוי may donate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי may also donate birds, wine, frankincense and wood for the מזבח.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן answers רב שיזבי by saying the sources follow a מחלוקת between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא. The ברייתא learns from 'איש איש' that a גוי can bring offerings. Its extra words include שלמים, תודה, birds, wine, frankincense and wood.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: 'Burnt Offering' Only Excludes a Nazir's Offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק says 'עולה' if a גוי can bring all kinds of offerings. רבי יוסי הגלילי answers that it comes to exclude the offering of a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say 'burnt offering'? 'Burnt offering' comes to exclude naziriteship. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question on its own reading and gives רבי יוסי הגלילי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9-10 showed that a גוי can bring שלמים, תודה, birds, wine and more. So why does the פסוק mention only 'עולה'? רבי יוסי הגלילי says the word is not limiting. It only excludes the עולה a נזיר brings, because a גוי cannot be a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the verse come to teach? (why is this word written?)
To exclude...
Being a נזיר: a vow to avoid wine, haircuts and impurity from the dead, ending with קרבנות

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say 'burnt offering'?
phrases.notes: 'If so' means: if a גוי can bring all those other offerings (steps 9-10). The פסוק is ויקרא 22:18.

phrases.english: 'Burnt offering' — to exclude naziriteship.
These are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading of the ברייתא by explaining the word 'עולה'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, a גוי may bring any offering except the offering of a נזיר.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: A Gentile Brings Only a Burnt Offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads the same פסוק as limiting: a גוי may bring only an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'Which they will offer to ה׳ as a burnt offering': I only have a burnt offering alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the other side of the מחלוקת: רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the word 'לעולה' limits a גוי to an עולה only. So a גוי's מנחה would not be accepted. That is why רבי יוחנן in step 7 said the rule from step 1 (a גוי's שלמים become עולות) follows רבי עקיבא, while the משנה about a גוי's מנחה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי.

keyTerms.meaning: Alone, only

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי: a גוי brings almost every offering (except a נזיר's). רבי עקיבא: a גוי brings only an עולה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
'Which they will offer to ה׳ as a burnt offering':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:18

phrases.english: I only have a burnt offering alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same פסוק, completing the מחלוקת that רבי יוחנן pointed to in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, a גוי may bring only an עולה.

steps.title: Isn't the Exclusion of Nazirite Already Learned Elsewhere?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why do we need the word 'עולה' to exclude a גוי from נזירות, when the פסוק about נזיר already says only בני ישראל can make that vow?
steps.simpleTranslation: And is this exclusion of naziriteship learned from here? It is learned from there: 'Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: a man who clearly utters a vow of a nazirite to separate himself': the children of Israel make the vow, but the gentiles do not make the vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading, because another פסוק already seems to teach the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי used the word 'עולה' to exclude a גוי's נזיר offering. But the פסוק in במדבר says 'בני ישראל', which already shows that a גוי cannot become a נזיר. If he can't be a נזיר, he would never bring a נזיר's offering, so the word 'עולה' seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it learned from here?
It is learned from there (another source)
They make a vow

phrases.english: And this exclusion of naziriteship,
is it learned from here?
It is learned from there:
'Speak to the children of Israel and say to them:
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:2

phrases.aramaic: אִישׁ כִּי יַפְלִא לִנְדֹּר נֶדֶר נָזִיר לְהַזִּיר״
phrases.english: a man who clearly utters a vow of a nazirite, to separate himself'
The children of Israel make the vow,
but the gentiles do not make the vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source רבי יוסי הגלילי used in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's use of 'עולה' to exclude נזירות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק in במדבר ('בני ישראל') already excludes a גוי from נזירות, so a second source seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Both Sources Are Needed: Not Just the Offering, but Nazirite Status Itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the offering verse alone would only block the קרבן. We might still think a גוי can become a נזיר, so the נזיר verse teaches that נזירות does not take effect on him at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were only from there, I would have said: it is the offering that he cannot bring, but naziriteship does take effect on them. The verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each פסוק teaches something different, so neither one is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An exclusion that only talks about offerings would only stop a גוי from bringing the קרבן. We might still think his נזיר vow is valid and he must keep the נזיר rules. The פסוק 'בני ישראל' teaches that the vow itself does not take effect on a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
Takes effect upon them
It teaches us (the new point)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the two פסוקים teach the same thing. One deals with the קרבן, and the other deals with whether the גוי becomes a נזיר at all.

phrases.english: If it were from there, I would have said:
phrases.notes: 'There' here means the verse about offerings. That verse by itself would only rule out the קרבן.

phrases.english: it is the offering that they may not bring,
but naziriteship does take effect upon them.
It teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by showing each source teaches a different point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both sources are needed: each teaches a different point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the offering exclusion, a גוי could not bring the קרבן but would still become a נזיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The נזיר verse teaches that נזירות does not take effect on a גוי at all.

steps.title: Whose View Does the משנה About a Gentile's Libations Follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה in שקלים follows. That משנה says a גוי's עולה sent from overseas is offered with נסכים, paid by him or by the public.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this משנה follow? רבי שמעון said: The court set up seven ordinances, and this is one of them: a גוי who sent his burnt offering from overseas and sent its libations with it, they are offered from his money. If not, they are offered from public funds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new related question. It quotes a משנה and gets ready to figure out which side of the מחלוקת it follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that a גוי's עולה comes with נסכים (wine libations). רבי עקיבא said a גוי brings only an עולה, so the question is whether the משנה can fit his view. It may only fit רבי יוסי הגלילי. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does it follow?
The court enacted (set up a rule)
Wine (with flour and oil) offerings that go along with a קרבן
A faraway land overseas
From public funds (the מקדש treasury)

phrases.english: Whose view does this, which we learned in a משנה, follow?
Rabbi Shimon said:
The court enacted seven things,
and this is one of them:
phrases.notes: 'This' points back to the rule right before it in that משנה: a found animal's נסכים are paid by the public.

phrases.english: A gentile who sent his burnt offering from overseas
and sent its libations along with it:
they are offered from his own money.
And if not, they are offered from public funds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting up the מחלוקת, the גמרא tests which side a known משנה follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the משנה about a גוי's עולה with נסכים follow רבי יוסי הגלילי or רבי עקיבא?

steps.title: Suggesting the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the משנה in שקלים follows רבי יוסי הגלילי and not רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, and not רבי עקיבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer to the question from the last step. It suggests the משנה about a גוי's עולה with נסכים follows רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי lets a גוי bring all kinds of offerings, so נסכים are no problem for him. רבי עקיבא said a גוי may bring only an עולה, and נסכים seem to be something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say: a suggested answer that the גמרא may later reject

phrases.english: Let us say it is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
phrases.notes: "It" means the משנה in שקלים from the last step, about a גוי's עולה sent from overseas.

phrases.english: and not Rabbi Akiva!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, וְלָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a tentative answer to the שאלה in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the משנה in שקלים follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Tentatively, רבי יוסי הגלילי, because רבי עקיבא limits a גוי to an עולה alone.

steps.title: It can fit רבי עקיבא too: an עולה with its accessories
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Even רבי עקיבא allows an עולה along with everything that goes with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it is רבי עקיבא. He allows an עולה and all its accessories.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 16. The משנה can fit רבי עקיבא as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When רבי עקיבא said 'only an עולה', he meant the עולה as a full package, including the נסכים that normally come with it. So the משנה does not contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say: the case fits the opinion we thought it went against
Its accessories: the things that normally come along with it

phrases.english: You can even say it is Rabbi Akiva:
a burnt offering and all its (companions) [accessories].
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא has the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the word in square brackets. Either way, it means everything that goes with the עולה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion that the משנה cannot fit רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה in שקלים follows only רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed רבי עקיבא's 'only an עולה' leaves out the נסכים that come with it.

steps.title: Who taught the ברייתא about a גוי and נסכים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא taught a ברייתא: a גוי cannot bring נסכים on their own, but his עולה still needs נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught this ברייתא? The פסוק says 'אזרח': a Jew can bring נסכים, but a גוי cannot bring נסכים. Might you think a גוי's עולה needs no נסכים? The פסוק says 'ככה', meaning every offering needs them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא and asks which תנא it follows. This sets up the difficulty in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes two points. A גוי cannot donate נסכים as an offering on their own. Yet when he brings an עולה, it still needs its normal נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: Home-born: here, a Jew
So, in this way: teaches that every such offering gets נסכים
Requires

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who taught this
that the Rabbis taught:
"Home-born": a home-born brings libations,
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:13

phrases.english: but a gentile does not bring libations.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא תְּהֵא עוֹלָתוֹ טְעוּנָה נְסָכִים?
phrases.english: One might think his burnt offering does not require libations?
The verse teaches: "So."
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:11

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה in שקלים to a second source, asking the same 'which תנא' question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא, רבי יוסי הגלילי or רבי עקיבא, the ברייתא about נסכים follows.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to fit neither תנא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא does not seem to match רבי יוסי הגלילי, who allows even wine, or רבי עקיבא, who allows only an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is it? Not רבי יוסי הגלילי's and not רבי עקיבא's. רבי יוסי הגלילי said a גוי may bring even wine. רבי עקיבא said only an עולה, and nothing else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא clashes with both opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Against רבי יוסי הגלילי: he allows a גוי to bring wine on its own, but the ברייתא forbids נסכים on their own. Against רבי עקיבא: he allows nothing besides an עולה, but the ברייתא gives the גוי's עולה נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is it?
Wine, brought as its own offering
Anything else

phrases.english: Whose view is it?

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי וְלָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: Not Rabbi Yosei HaGelili and not Rabbi Akiva.
If it is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
he said even wine too!
phrases.notes: He means a גוי can bring wine as its own offering, not just as part of an עולה.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Akiva, he said:
a burnt offering, yes;
anything else, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? לָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי וְלָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens the question of step 18 into a real difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: Matching the ברייתא to either רבי יוסי הגלילי or רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ban on נסכים alone goes against רבי יוסי הגלילי (who allows wine). Giving נסכים to the עולה goes against רבי עקיבא (only an עולה).

steps.title: It can fit either תנא
steps.stepSummary: Either take 'wine' out of רבי יוסי הגלילי's ברייתא, or read רבי עקיבא as allowing an עולה with all its accessories.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is רבי יוסי הגלילי, or if you want, say it is רבי עקיבא. If רבי יוסי הגלילי: remove 'wine' from that ברייתא. If רבי עקיבא: he allows an עולה and all its accessories.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא can match either תנא, and it gives a fix for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, we delete 'wine' from the earlier ברייתא, so he never let a גוי bring wine alone. For רבי עקיבא, we use the same idea as step 17: the נסכים are part of the עולה package.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove from that one: take a word out of the earlier text

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי may not bring נסכים as their own offering, but his עולה gets its normal נסכים. רבי עקיבא's 'only an עולה' includes everything that comes with the עולה.

phrases.english: If you want, say it is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili;
and if you want, say it is Rabbi Akiva.
If you want, say it is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili:
remove "wine" from that one,
phrases.notes: "That one" is the ברייתא that quoted רבי יוסי הגלילי allowing wine.

phrases.english: and if you want, say it is Rabbi Akiva:
a burnt offering and all its (companions) [accessories].

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 19 with two possible answers.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two alternative answers: change the wording of the earlier ברייתא, or reread רבי עקיבא's limit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא fits neither תנא, because one allows wine alone and the other allows only a bare עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבי יוסי הגלילי, 'wine' is removed from his ברייתא. Under רבי עקיבא, the עולה includes its נסכים.

steps.title: Where does רבי שמעון's rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's statement in the משנה about a כהן's מנחת חוטא and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי שמעון says a sinner's meal offering brought by כהנים is treated in a special way. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It quotes רבי שמעון's line from the משנה and asks for the source, which sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal מנחה brought by a כהן is burned completely on the מזבח. רבי שמעון says a כהן's מנחת חוטא follows its own special procedure. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner's meal offering, brought by a poor person who cannot afford an animal for certain sins
From where do we know these things? A request for the source

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים [וְכוּ׳].
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: The sinner's meal offering of priests, etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of a גוי's offerings and starts a new piece of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that is the source for רבי שמעון's rule about a כהן's מנחת חוטא.

steps.title: The ברייתא: the כהן may do the service himself
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "וְהָיְתָה לַכֹּהֵן כַּמִּנְחָה" that the עבודה of a כהן's מנחת חוטא is valid when he does it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Sages taught: "And it shall be the priest's, as the meal offering." This teaches that its service is valid when done by him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא. Its first reading of the פסוק is that a כהן may do the עבודה of his own מנחת חוטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "וְהָיְתָה לַכֹּהֵן כַּמִּנְחָה" seem extra, so the ברייתא uses them to teach a new rule. A כהן who sinned may personally do the עבודה on the מנחה that atones for him.

keyTerms.meaning: The service of the offering, such as taking the handful and burning it
Valid when done by him, meaning the כהן who brought it

phrases.english: As the Sages taught: "And it shall be the priest's, as the meal offering,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:13

phrases.english: that its service should be valid by him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "וְהָיְתָה לַכֹּהֵן כַּמִּנְחָה" teaches that the כהן may do the עבודה of his own מנחת חוטא.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means a כהן's required מנחה is eaten
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests another reading: the verse lets a כהן's מנחת חוטא be eaten, and the rule that a כהן's מנחה is fully burned covers only his voluntary מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say the verse teaches that its service is valid by him? Or maybe it only comes to permit eating the sinner's meal offering of priests. Then how do I explain "Every meal offering of a priest shall be completely burned, it shall not be eaten"? That would be about his voluntary meal offering, but his required one may be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own reading. Maybe the פסוק is really saying that a כהן's מנחת חוטא may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other פסוק says every מנחה of a כהן is fully burned. The suggestion limits that rule to a נדבה (voluntary offering). That would leave the חובה (required offering) free to be eaten, just like a regular person's מנחת חוטא.

keyTerms.meaning: A voluntary offering that a person chooses to bring
A required offering that a person must bring
Completely burned on the מזבח
Then how do I explain (another פסוק that seems to contradict)?

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר שֶׁתְּהֵא עֲבוֹדָתָהּ כְּשֵׁרָה בּוֹ,
phrases.english: Do you say that its service should be valid by him,
or is it only to permit
the sinner's meal offering of priests,
phrases.notes: Meaning: to permit it to be eaten, like a regular person's.

phrases.english: and how do I uphold

phrases.aramaic: ״וְכׇל מִנְחַת כֹּהֵן כָּלִיל תִּהְיֶה לֹא תֵאָכֵל״?
phrases.english: "And every meal offering of a priest shall be completely burned; it shall not be eaten"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:16

phrases.english: That is his voluntary meal offering,
but his required one may be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר שֶׁתְּהֵא עֲבוֹדָתָהּ כְּשֵׁרָה בּוֹ, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in Step 22 by offering a different meaning for the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that "וְהָיְתָה לַכֹּהֵן כַּמִּנְחָה" teaches the כהן may do the עבודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could instead mean a כהן's required מנחה is eaten. The rule "כָּלִיל תִּהְיֶה" would then cover only his voluntary מנחה.

steps.title: The verse compares his required מנחה to his voluntary one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that "כַּמִּנְחָה" compares the כהן's required מנחה to his voluntary מנחה, so neither one is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says "And it shall be the priest's, as the meal offering." It compares his required offering to his voluntary offering. Just as his voluntary offering is not eaten, so too his required offering is not eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the suggestion that a כהן's מנחת חוטא is eaten. It explains the word "כַּמִּנְחָה" as a comparison to his voluntary מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse links (מַקִּישׁ) the כהן's required מנחה to his voluntary one, which is never eaten. So the required one is not eaten either. The verse cannot be about permitting eating, which leaves the first reading in place: the כהן may do the עבודה himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares, linking two things in the פסוק so they share the same law (a הֶקֵּשׁ)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves of the ברייתא. Steps 22 to 24 are the first (anonymous) view. רבי שמעון only starts speaking in the next step, and he disagrees with this reading.

phrases.english: The verse states: "And it shall be the priest's, as the meal offering,"
comparing his required offering to his voluntary offering:
just as his voluntary offering is not eaten,
so too his required offering is not eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A הֶקֵּשׁ that blocks the other reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן's required מנחת חוטא might be eaten, and only his voluntary מנחה is fully burned.
steps.terutzMaskana: "כַּמִּנְחָה" compares his required מנחה to his voluntary one, so neither is eaten.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the verse says "the מנחה," not "his מנחה"
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rejects the comparison to the כהן's own voluntary מנחה. The verse says "כַּמִּנְחָה," not "כְּמִנְחָתוֹ," so it must be comparing to a different מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: Does it say "And it shall be the priest's, as HIS meal offering"? It only says "as THE meal offering"! Rather, it comes to compare...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון argues with the ברייתא's reading. He starts to give his own explanation of what the פסוק compares, and that explanation continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view read "כַּמִּנְחָה" as "like his own voluntary מנחה." רבי שמעון points out that the פסוק would have said "כְּמִנְחָתוֹ" if it meant the כהן's own מנחה. Since it says "the מנחה," it is comparing to some other מנחה, and this is where his rule in the משנה comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it actually say...? Pointing to wording that is not in the פסוק
Like HIS meal offering, the wording the פסוק does not use
But surely..., introducing what the פסוק really says

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the real source for רבי שמעון's rule in the משנה. His whole view depends on the small difference between "כַּמִּנְחָה" and "כְּמִנְחָתוֹ."

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
Is it stated, "And it shall be the priest's, as his meal offering"?
But it says only "as the meal offering"!
phrases.notes: "The" מנחה means a general one, not the כהן's own, so it can't be his voluntary מנחה.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to compare
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished yet. רבי שמעון tells us what is being compared in the next lines of the daf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הֶקֵּשׁ in Step 24 and starts a different reading of the same פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The first view's reading that "כַּמִּנְחָה" means the כהן's own voluntary מנחה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק says "כַּמִּנְחָה" (the מנחה), not "כְּמִנְחָתוֹ" (his מנחה), so it cannot refer to the כהן's own offering.
